notes.trap: `element_at(...)` on an array is 1-based, but the `arr[i]` subscript is 0-based, so the same number picks different elements. With ANSI off (the default), an index past the end returns NULL instead of raising an error, while index 0 always raises an error.
The try_ prefix does not cover every error: index 0 still raises an error. Only out-of-range indexes and missing map keys return NULL.
notes.actual: ERROR: SparkRuntimeException INVALID_INDEX_OF_ZERO :: [INVALID_INDEX_OF_ZERO] The index 0 is invalid. An index shall be either < 0 or > 0 (the first element has index 1).

notes.trap: Duplicate keys do not use last-wins by default. With spark.sql.mapKeyDedupPolicy=EXCEPTION (the default), building a map with a repeated key raises an error, and so does a NULL key.
notes.actual: ERROR: SparkRuntimeException DUPLICATED_MAP_KEY :: [DUPLICATED_MAP_KEY] Duplicate map key 1 was found, please check the input data. If you want to remove the duplicated keys, you can set "spark.sql.mapKeyDedupPolicy" to "LAST_WIN" so that the key inserted at last takes precedence.

notes.trap: If any argument is a NULL map, the whole result is NULL; NULL maps are not skipped. A key that appears in more than one input map raises an error under the default dedup policy instead of keeping the last value.
notes.example_sql: SELECT map_concat(map(1, 'a'), CAST(NULL AS MAP<INT, STRING>))

notes.trap: A NULL element in the keys array raises an error rather than being dropped. Duplicate keys also raise an error under the default dedup policy.
notes.actual: ERROR: SparkRuntimeException NULL_MAP_KEY :: [NULL_MAP_KEY] Cannot use null as map key.

notes.trap: If the input array contains a NULL struct entry, the whole result is NULL; the NULL entry is not skipped.

Both delimiters are regular expressions, so regex metacharacters such as '|' or '.' must be escaped or wrapped in a character class. All values come back as STRING, and a pair with no key/value delimiter gets a NULL value.
